Pick up issue #113 in super-star-trek: sst.doc documents -t and its 72x24 minimum around lines 1544-1547 but says nothing    
  about resizing. All of that behaviour is only in README.md, and sst.doc is the manual reached from inside the game — so the  
  players most likely to drag a window can't see it.                                                                           
                                                                                                                               
  Follow the workflow in AGENTS.md, including checking the issue's premises before building on them.                           
                                                                                                                               
  Three things worth knowing up front:                                                                                         
                                                                                                                               
  1. sst.doc is CRLF and the game reads it at runtime. Under curses a trailing \r returns the cursor to column 0 and the       
  newline erases the line. sst.c:662 strips it. Verify new text through the in-game help, not just in an editor.               
  2. ui-review binds — this is text the game prints, not an instruction file.                                                  
  3. The content already exists and is reviewed. README.md's resize paragraphs went through several review rounds and are      
  accurate as of commit fef362c. The manual wants the player-facing consequences, not the reasoning about why the conversation 
  can't be rebuilt — don't copy them wholesale.                                                                                
                                                                                                                               
  Two specifics that took real work to establish, so don't re-derive or contradict them: the line you're on usually comes back 
  on a resize, but a question you'd already started answering does not (that's #117). At that one, tell the player to press    
  Ctrl-U before answering — a yes/no prompt reads the first letter, so an unseen y in the buffer makes a typed N mean yes, and 
  that can end the game.                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                               
  When you run the TUI test suite, run it as sh tests/tui.sh ./build/sst Debug. Without that second argument the sensors block 
  is silently skipped.
I'll start by inspecting the repo state and the issue.

`sst.doc` documents the `-t` option and its 72x24 minimum at lines 1544-1547, but
says nothing about what happens when the terminal is resized while the game is
running. All of that behaviour is documented only in `README.md`.

## Why it matters

`sst.doc` is what a player reaches from inside the game — it is the manual the
game itself points at. `README.md` is what someone reads on the repository page
before they have played. So the audience most likely to resize a window mid-game
is the one that cannot see any of this.

What is missing from the manual, all of it currently true and all of it in
`README.md`:

- resizing is safe at any point, including while the game waits for an answer
  or for a keystroke at a pause
- below 72x24 the panels clip rather than rearrange, and a clipped line ends in
  `>` so a shortened number is not mistaken for a small one
- growing back brings the panels with it however far the squeeze went, but the
  conversation that scrolled away is gone
- the line you are on usually comes back whole; a few prompts do not, and Enter
  re-prompts

## Scope

Pre-existing and untouched by the fix for #100, which is where it was noticed.

## Fix sketch

A short paragraph in the manual's `-t` section. It should not duplicate
`README.md` wholesale — the manual wants the player-facing consequences, not the
reasoning about why the conversation cannot be rebuilt.

Note that `sst.doc` is CRLF and is read by the game at runtime, so anything
added there is subject to the trailing-carriage-return rule in `AGENTS.md`.

## Provenance

Found by the `ui-review` sub-agent while reviewing #100's fix. Filed rather than
fixed there, per AGENTS.md step 9.

# Super Star Trek

Super Star Trek is an old text-only game, an early example of a turn-based space strategy sim, written in BASIC. In this game, you are the captain of the starship Enterprise, and your mission is to scout the federation space and eliminate all the invading Klingon ships. You will have to manage the ship energy carefully, use phasers and torpedoes to destroy the Klingons, and find starbases to repair damages and replenish your energy. All of this, rendered with a few characters on screen and a lot of imagination.

Super Star Trek is probably the most famous early text-only game ever created and it inspired many other videogames. Since the code was public domain, during the years, it was changed and improved many times. There are literally thousands of versions out there. All of them are nice, but my preference goes to the classic 1978 version called Super Star Trek.

[Read more about Star Trek and Super Star Trek.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Trek_%281971_video_game%29)

### Full-screen mode

Run `sst -t` for a full-screen interface: the short-range scan and the
ship's status stay on screen in two panels while the usual game
conversation scrolls below them. It needs a terminal of at least 72x24
and can be combined with the fixed-coordinate option (`sst -f -t`).
Without `-t` the game uses its classic scrolling display.

Resizing the terminal is fine at any point. The display follows it
straight away — while the game is waiting for you to answer, and while
it is waiting for a keystroke at a pause — and both the question you
were asked and the answer you were halfway through typing survive, so
long as there is still room for them. Older text that no longer fits
scrolls away, as it would in any terminal.

Dragged smaller than the 72x24 the panels ask for, they clip rather
than rearrange themselves. A line with more to show than there is room
for ends in `>`, so a shortened number is never mistaken for a small
one, and a heading with no room left is dropped rather than shortened.
A terminal shorter than the panels themselves loses rows off the bottom
of them, the grid keeping its numbering so you can see where it stops.

Shorter than fourteen rows there is no room left for the conversation
at all: the panels are the whole screen and the prompt is not on it.
Just above that there is barely more — at fourteen rows the one line
left over goes entirely to the pager, so a scan pages past without
showing any of itself; at fifteen it comes one line at a time.

Growing the terminal back brings the panels with it, however far the
squeeze went: they redraw from the game state, so they return full of
live readings. The conversation cannot be rebuilt that way — curses
does not reflow it — so whatever scrolled away while the window was
small is gone for good, and an older line that was cut short stays cut
short. Every reading is a command away, though, and none of them costs
anything: `srscan`, `status`, `chart`, `damages`.

The line you are on usually comes back, and it is the one that matters:
a question or a pause the game was part way through writing is written
out again whole once there is room for it, so you are not left typing
into the tail of a prompt. A few prompts finish their line before they
stop to wait; those come back too, with the answer going on the row
below the question — or after it, where the window is down to its last
row.
Only their final line comes back, so a question asked over several
lines returns as the last of them. The one gap left is a question you
have already started answering: that one is left exactly as it was
before, so what comes back may be a stump of older conversation, or
nothing, with the game still waiting behind it.

Do not just answer that one, and do not press Enter either: whatever
you typed is still in the buffer, and a yes/no question reads the
*first* letter, so an `N` typed after a `y` you cannot see answers yes.

#112 restores a prompt that ended its own line — `prout` appends the newline, so
`curline` is empty by the time the reader waits, and the question used to vanish
on a resize. The fix keeps the finished line and puts it back.

It deliberately does **not** do so once the player has begun typing.

## Why

An ended prompt and its part-typed answer occupy two rows, with curses' padding
between them. `restore_curline()` compares against a single joined string, and
spanning that boundary went wrong twice in review:

- Leaving the answer out of the comparison meant the tail test never fired, so a
  drag reprinted the question **once per width step** — copies stacking up the
  window, which is the exact failure `restore_curline()`'s comparison exists to
  prevent.
- Padding the answer back to the row boundary fixed that and turned a one-row
  height shrink (80x24 → 80x23) into a **second copy** instead.

Both were found by `ui-review`; the second was my fix for the first.

## What happens now

With an answer part typed, an ended prompt is left alone on a resize — the
behaviour before #112. The answer itself is still restored by the ordinary
`curline` path, so the player can see what they have typed; the question above
it is at worst truncated, exactly as it was.

That is milder than either failure above, which is why it is the state that
ships. It is still worth fixing.

## Fix sketch

The comparison needs to model two rows rather than one. Either:

cat > "$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/issue.md" <<'EOF'
`helpme()` (`sst.c:127-199`) is the only thing that opens `sst.doc`, and it
prints exactly one shape of entry. It builds a key of `  Mnemonic:  <COMMAND>`
— or ` ABBREV` for the abbreviation table — scans forward for the first line
carrying that prefix, and prints until a line containing `******`.

So the only text `help` can reach is a command entry. The last one is
`  Mnemonic:  SCORE` at `sst.doc:1294`, and the `ABBREV` table is at
`sst.doc:1406`. Everything after that is unreachable from inside the game:

- `MISCELLANEOUS NOTES` (1302) — black holes, the Neutral Zone, ramming
  commanders, how fast the Super-commander travels
- `SCORING` (1349) — the whole scoring table
- `MODIFICATIONS` (1471), which includes the full-screen `-t` section at
  1541 and everything #113 is adding to it
- `ACKNOWLEDGMENTS` (1552) and `REFERENCES` (1573)

## Why it matters

The game names `sst.doc` to the player and refuses to give help without it
("You need to find SST.DOC and put it in the current directory", `sst.c:163`),
which reads as a promise that the file is the manual the game will show you.
It shows you a fifth of it. A player who wants to know what the scoring
actually is, or what happens when they drag the window, has to leave the game
and open the file in a pager.

This is what makes #113's premise only half true — the manual is the right
home for that text, but adding it there does not put it in front of a player
mid-game.

## How to see it

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug && cmake --build build
printf 'regular\nshort\nnovice\nxyz\nhelp score\n' | ./build/sst
```

`help score` prints the `SCORE` *command* entry (`sst.doc:1294`), not the
`SCORING` section (1349). There is no argument at all that reaches 1541.

## Fix sketch

`help` would need a way to name a topic that is not a command. Either a
second key shape in `helpme()` — a `  Topic:  <NAME>` line placed above the
narrative sections, terminated the same way — or a `help display` /
`help scoring` special-cased the way ` ABBREV` already is at `sst.c:152-154`.
Whichever it is, `listCommands()` and the `HELP` entry in `sst.doc` would
have to say the topics exist, or nobody will guess them.

## Provenance

Found while doing #113, checking the claim that `sst.doc` is what a player
reaches from inside the game. Filed rather than fixed there, per AGENTS.md
step 9.
EOF
gh issue create --title "Most of sst.doc is unreachable from in-game help" --body-file "$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/issue.md"

**The `-t` section is at `sst.doc:1541-1549`, not 1544-1547.** Line 1544 does

option and 1547-1549 are the fallback notice. The new text goes after 1549.

this section.** `helpme()` (`sst.c:127-199`) is the only thing that opens the
file, and it prints one shape of entry: it builds `  Mnemonic:  <COMMAND>`
(or ` ABBREV`), scans for the first line with that prefix, and prints until a
line containing `******`. The last such entry is `  Mnemonic:  SCORE` at
`sst.doc:1294`; the `ABBREV` table is at 1406. Everything after that —
`MISCELLANEOUS NOTES`, `SCORING`, `MODIFICATIONS` (where the `-t` section
lives), `ACKNOWLEDGMENTS`, `REFERENCES` — is never printed by the game. A
player reaches this text by opening the file, not with `help`.

That narrows the "Why it matters" argument rather than voiding it. `sst.doc`
still ships with the game, still has to sit in the working directory for
`help` to work at all, and is still where a player looks rather than at a
repository page — so the manual remains the right home for this, and the fix
sketch stands as written. The reachability gap itself is now #120.

**"the line you are on usually comes back whole; a few prompts do not, and
Enter re-prompts" conflates two cases, and for one of them the advice is
dangerous.** What is actually true:

- *Prompt missing or cut short, nothing typed yet.* Enter is safe. A pause
  moves on, the self-destruct password reads an empty answer as a refusal,
  and a yes/no question comes back as `Please answer with "Y" or "N":`.
- *An answer already part typed.* The question is not put back at all (#117),

  first token of the line and tests `*citem == 'y'`, so a `y` still sitting

  lowercases to "yn" and returns TRUE. The player has to press Ctrl-U
  (`tui.c:920`) first. Some of those questions cost the game: `events.c:420`
  asks "Are you sure?" before resting past your remaining time, or with
  enemies in the quadrant.

The paragraph as written tells the player to press Ctrl-U in the second case,
and keeps Enter for the first, where it is safe.

question and the answer, and what is left at the bottom of the window is
whatever older conversation the squeeze brought into view.

answer both gone, reader still waiting, an old long-range scan sitting where
the prompt should be.

failures it was chosen over. It also raises the stakes on the recovery advice:
because nothing is restored, the player cannot tell from the screen that a
reader is waiting at all, which is why the manual paragraph added in #113

Merged. `main` is at `2f7f06d`, #113 is closed, branch deleted.

## What shipped

Four paragraphs in `sst.doc`'s `-t` section (46 lines, CRLF), covering what the manual never said about resizing a running game: that a resize never crashes the game or drops it back to the classic display; how the display gives way — panel lines clipping with a `>` marker below 72 columns, the conversation running out at fifteen, fourteen and thirteen rows *before* the panels lose rows of their own; what growing back restores and what it can't; and what to do at a prompt a resize has swallowed — press Ctrl-U before answering, because `ja()` reads the first letter of the first word and an `N` typed after an unseen `y` answers yes.

## Two things you should know

**The issue's central premise was wrong, and I built anyway.** `sst.doc` is *not* reachable from inside the game for this section — `helpme()` prints only per-command entries keyed by `  Mnemonic:  <COMMAND>` / ` ABBREV`, and the last one terminates 79 lines above the insertion point. So your instruction to "verify new text through the in-game help" couldn't be followed directly. I verified rendering by splicing the paragraphs into a real `SRSCAN` help entry in a scratch copy of the tree, building fresh there, and paging under curses at 72x24 and 80x24. The manual is still the right home (it ships with the binary and must sit in the working directory for `help` to work at all), so the slice stood — corrected on #113 by comment, gap filed as #120.

**`ui-review` took six rounds**, and rounds 1–2 found eight substantive errors, not style. The ones worth naming: the starbase locations were *not* an unrecoverable loss (`CHART` has them from setup, `setup.c:339`), the height thresholds were inverted, and the `>` marker is width-only. Rounds 3–6 came back clean; I cut off round 6 explicitly after three consecutive "acceptable as-is" verdicts were producing nits about the previous round's own wording.

## Issues filed

| | |
|---|---|
| #120 | Most of `sst.doc` is unreachable from in-game `help` |
| #121 | `MODIFICATIONS` has outgrown its page number (125 lines vs a 47–67 band; 81 before this) |
| #122 | README's resize section over-promises, then contradicts itself |
| #123 | Nothing ties the 15/14/13-row thresholds to their behaviour (verifier's finding) |

Plus a comment on **#117** correcting its body: with an ended prompt and a part-typed answer, a resize loses *both* the question and the answer — `tui_readline()` echoes with `waddch` and never calls `note_out()`, so `restore_curline()` returns at `tui.c:436` having restored nothing.

**No test was added** — the text is prose in a region no command can print, proved rather than assumed (the verifier diffed all 38 `help` outputs across the change and found them byte-identical). Six resolved-not-fixed findings are recorded in the PR body. On your note about test scope: the main agent ran only the two compiled unit tests (`tuifmt`, `rules`); the full battery ran in the `verifier`, and CI passed all four jobs.
